A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete, readable versions of the same study, including Table 1, Figures 1–22, and Appendices A–J. Text and visual inspection support reliable comparison despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original localization and ablation experiments covering 67 English syntactic phenomena in seven LLMs, multilingual analyses using Gemma, and additional empirical results in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original localization, ablation, and multilingual results in Sections 4.1–4.3 and Appendices A–J.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 retains the same localization procedure using last-token activation magnitudes, Welch t-statistics, and top-ranked units. Residual-stream and module analyses and the ablation procedures are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both use BLiMP, SyntaxGym, Gulordava and Linzen materials, RuBLiMP, SLING, and MultiBLiMP. Coverage retains the same 90-language overlap analysis and 57-language syntactic-similarity subset.

E2.justification: Random, BLiMP-Control, BLiMP-Lex, and random-unit ablation comparisons retain their participation in the corresponding experiments. The newly cited papers do not introduce evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: Table 1 retains the same seven model configurations. Localization thresholds, the 500/500 BLiMP localization/evaluation split, overlap and accuracy metrics, and appendix evaluation protocols are unchanged.

E4.justification: The threshold sensitivity tests, module/layer breakdowns, five-fold validation, cross-benchmark generalization, mean-ablation checks, correlation analyses, and lexical controls are retained. Appendix reflow adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Four-seed random-ablation reporting and 95% confidence intervals over models in Figure 2 are unchanged. Significance tests and correlation reporting also retain the same procedures.

E6.justification: Main and appendix results match, including average ablation drops of 7.61% versus 1.68% in Section 4.1, mean-ablation drops of 7.88% versus 5.82% in Appendix F, and Spearman correlation 0.460 in Figure 8. Plotted content is unchanged.

T1.justification: The overlap calculations and BLiMP-Lex averaging formula in Appendix I are unchanged. No mathematical definition, formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: Section 5 weakens the conclusion from results that 'rule out the possibility' of generic syntax-processing units to results that 'argue against the idea.' The abstract and three stated main contributions otherwise retain their claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 makes the interpretation concerning generic syntax-processing units less categorical. Existing limitations concerning localization, activation basis, and causal interpretation remain unchanged; the proposed human multilingual follow-up is reorganized but retained.

D1.justification: The disclosed model specifications, localization and ablation implementation details, module recording locations, BLiMP-Lex construction instructions, and first-page code/data link are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography add Lu et al. (2025) on multilingual factual-recall interventions and Ruochen Zhang et al. (2025) on multilingual structural similarities. This modestly expands related-work coverage without redefining the research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited copyedits, streamlines the discussion, consolidates the human multilingual research suggestion, and corrects the duplicated section-reference notation in Limitations. The overall section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: Several appendix figures are resized and repositioned within the existing two-column layout. Figure 9 moves from PDF page 13 to 14, and Figure 19 from page 17 to 18. Table 1, all 22 figures, captions, and plotted content are retained.

improvement.justification: Changing 'rule out' to 'argue against' in Section 5 better matches the acknowledged limitations of top-n% localization. Added multilingual related work and lighter discussion editing modestly improve context and clarity. The empirical evidence and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
